Slots.maps_to: TwoTailedRatsNormal.cs:12: ['first','second','third','fourth','fifth']. Sim: Encounter.slots defaults to the empty tuple (monsters/base.py:371) and TwoTailedRatsEncounter (two_tailed_rat.py:140-158) never overrides it, so TWO_TAILED_RATS_NORMAL.slots == () at runtime.
Slots.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The `Encounter` dataclass already had `slots`/`monster_slots` and `CreatureCmd.add(slot_name=)` re-sorts on them (shipped round 7 for Fabricator/Ovicopter); this unit simply never declared its row. It does now, transcribed from the C# `Slots` override and `GenerateMonsters`' `(model, slot)` pairs, and `CombatState.__init__` routes every roster through `Encounter.seat_in_slots` so the seventeen `create_monsters` overrides are seated too. Regression tests: test/test_encounter_slots.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: encounter/_slot_order (G1, proposed shared mechanism id -- see report). Executed witness: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e8.py rat-slot-order`. The empty `slots` is harmless for the INITIAL roster: the 3 starting rats are just appended in GenerateMonsters' return order (two_tailed_rat.py:147-158), which already equals their C# slot order (Slots[2..4] = third/fourth/fifth, TwoTailedRatsNormal.cs:33-41) since nothing else occupies the row yet. It is NOT harmless for CALL_FOR_BACKUP: `TwoTailedRat._call_for_backup` (two_tailed_rat.py:129-137) calls `CreatureCmd.add(ctx.hooks, TwoTailedRat(...))` with no `slot_name`, so `cmds.py`'s `if slot_name is not None: ... combat.sort_enemies_by_slot_name()` (cmds.py:839-841) never runs and the summon is simply appended to the END of `combat.enemies`. The probe shows the sim's post-summon order is [rat(1), rat(2), rat(3), NEW(4)] by net_id, all with slot_name=None. C# (TwoTailedRat.cs:180-185) resolves `Encounter.Slots.LastOrDefault(s => no enemy has s)` (= 'second', the only two unoccupied slots being 'first'/'second') and `CreatureCmd.Add(combatState, 'second')` triggers `CombatManager.AddCreature`'s `SortEnemiesBySlotName`, which re-sorts the WHOLE `Enemies` list by `Slots.IndexOf(SlotName)` (CombatState.cs:495-501) -- the summon lands AHEAD of all three starting rats ('second' < 'third'/'fourth'/'fifth'). Net_id/CombatId is assigned in attach order regardless (cmds.py:828-834, so replay targeting by CombatId still resolves), but the `combat.enemies` INDEX order -- what the observation encoder positions enemies by and what `CombatCtx.resolve_target(target_idx)` (combat.py:109-113) reads for index-based targeting -- disagrees with the game from the first successful CALL_FOR_BACKUP onward. This is not a corner case: CALL_FOR_BACKUP is gated on `turns_until_summonable<=0` (2 acted turns) + a 75% per-eligible-turn roll + a free slot + no sibling already telegraphing one, which ordinary Underdocks fights reach by turn 3-4.

guards.what: encounter/_selection_rng_fallback (G2, proposed shared mechanism id -- see report): EncounterModel.Rng's documented per-encounter independence (EncounterModel.cs:42-48, 'independently of the run's centralized RNG... safe... because we don't need to keep track of a given encounter's RNG state once it's over') vs TwoTailedRatsEncounter.create_monsters' selection_rng fallback (two_tailed_rat.py:151-154)
guards.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). `RunState.create_combat` now builds the per-encounter Rng on BOTH paths: with a string seed from `rng_set.seed` as before, and without one from a run seed derived at construction (`run.derive_encounter_seed`, a hash of the shared generator's STATE, so it consumes no draw and shifts no other legacy stream). `create_monsters`' `selection_rng=None` arm is therefore unreachable from any production call site, and the composition no longer moves when the shared stream does — executed in test/test_encounter_selection_rng.py (test_the_composition_does_not_move_with_the_shared_stream) and by audit/tools/encounter_probes_e2.py legacy-shared-stream.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: Executed witness: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e8.py rat-selection-rng`. `RunState.create_combat` (run.py:1605-1619) only builds an independent `encounter_selection_rng` (via `make_encounter_rng`, seeded off `rng_set.seed + total_floor + entry`) when `self.rng_set is not None`, which itself requires a `string_seed` at `RunState.__init__` (run.py:170-176). The RL training path (`run_env.py:747`, inside `STS2RunEnv`) constructs `RunState(rng=self._rng, character=self._character)` with NO `string_seed`, so `rng_set` is None for every training episode, `encounter_selection_rng` is None, and `TwoTailedRatsEncounter.create_monsters` falls back to `rng.randrange(3)` on the SAME shared per-combat `random.Random` that every other unseeded draw in the fight consumes (two_tailed_rat.py:151-154). This is the 'stream named in C# but not honoured' shape (PROMPT.md bug class 16): EncounterModel.Rng's own doc comment says the independence is what makes the draw safe to leave untracked, but that is true only if the draw is actually off an independent stream -- in the trained configuration it is not, so this draw shifts every later unseeded draw in the same combat by one call relative to a hypothetical independent-Rng sim, in every two_tailed_rats_normal fight (the only encounter among these 10 units whose GenerateMonsters draws anything at all, but the same `selection_rng is None -> shared rng` fallback shape recurs at every other draw-consuming encounter in the kind -- see report for the cross-batch list).
